claims.text: Increasing Mn concentration in a magnetic high-entropy alloy can increase its coercive field.
The proposed intervention is the addition of Mn to a magnetic high-entropy alloy.
The intervention is intended to apply to as-cast or annealed magnetic high-entropy alloys.
The expected coercivity effect should occur at room temperature under an applied magnetic field.
Mn3+/Mn2+ oxidation states are the structural mediator of the proposed coercivity change.
Adding Mn can increase saturation magnetization in magnetic high-entropy alloys.
Adding Mn modifies magnetic anisotropy in a way relevant to coercivity.
The Mn-induced changes in saturation magnetization and magnetic anisotropy lead to increased coercive field.
The Mn-containing alloy should have a higher coercive field than an otherwise comparable alloy without Mn addition.
The proposed effect is limited to magnetic high-entropy alloys with similar composition and processing state.
The magnitude of the coercivity increase depends on alloy composition and processing conditions.
Failure of the Mn-containing alloy to show increased coercivity relative to the no-Mn control would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The target is described as a metallic high-entropy alloy, but the proposed Mn3+/Mn2+ mediator is an ionic oxidation-state concept associated with oxides, and both cited records concern ferrite or high-entropy oxide systems. No oxidized alloy state or oxide phase is specified.
